issues.legal_issue: A civil suit should not be stayed pending a related criminal prosecution merely because both proceedings may produce conflicting decisions when continuing the civil suit is unlikely to embarrass the defendants in the criminal case.
material_facts: A criminal prosecution was pending based on allegations that the defendants had forged a will and used it to obtain a mutation of disputed property.
A civil suit sought declarations of title, possession and injunction, and the annulment of a sale deed and mutation order; it also referred to the alleged forged will.
The defendants had filed their written statement in the civil suit, and the court had framed issues on the parties’ pleadings.
The Court found that continuing the civil suit would not prejudice the defendants’ defence in the criminal proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was not justified in staying the civil suit until the criminal case was decided. The stay was set aside, and the civil suit was to proceed in accordance with law.
issues.legal_principle: Under M.S. Sheriff v. State of Madras, no hard-and-fast rule determines which of simultaneous civil and criminal proceedings must be stayed; the possibility of conflicting decisions is not a relevant ground, while the likelihood of embarrassment is relevant and the circumstances of the particular case control. K.G. Premshanker v. Inspector of Police reaffirmed that principle and held that the effect of a judgment in one proceeding depends on its relevance under Sections 40–43 of the Evidence Act, 1872; a civil judgment is not generally conclusive in a criminal case except as provided by Section 41. State of Rajasthan v. Kalyan Sundaram Cement Industries also supports proceeding with civil litigation despite a pending criminal case. The contrary proposition in V.M. Shah v. State of Maharashtra was held not to be good law in K.G. Premshanker.

rule.if: civil_suit_and_criminal_prosecution_pending and civil_defence_filed and civil_issues_framed and not likely_criminal_defence_embarrassment

predicates.civil_suit_and_criminal_prosecution_pend: A civil suit and a related criminal prosecution are both pending.
predicates.civil_defence_filed: The defendants have filed their defence in the civil suit.
predicates.civil_issues_framed: The civil court has framed issues on the parties’ pleadings.
predicates.likely_criminal_defence_embarrassment: Continuing the civil suit is likely to embarrass the defendants in presenting their defence in the criminal case.
predicates.civil_suit_proceeds_without_waiting_for_: The civil suit proceeds without waiting for the criminal case to conclude.

issues.definition: When a civil suit and a related criminal prosecution are pending, the defendants have filed their civil defence, the civil issues have been framed, and continuing the suit is not likely to embarrass their criminal defence, the civil suit proceeds without waiting for the criminal case to conclude.
